analysis:
Integration review of the supplied units found no concrete security regression. The PR bumps three MLX submodule pins (libs/mlx ad4745a2 to ff4bb35b, libs/mlx-swift 67dc7528 to eedca444, libs/mlx-swift-lm 6148b6da to 476cb7c0), updates doc dates and the GatedDelta.swift path, and adapts provider and test code to the new SDK API.

Examined adaptations:
- GLM5NextProtectedExecution.swift:144-149: the new prepare signature still calls requireInput before delegating to root.prepare, so the context bound is preserved.
- MLXLLM-qualified Gemma4AssistantDraftModel.load calls in EngineV2MTPAssistant.swift, MTPProductionSession.swift and BackendParityHarness.swift.
- ModelBenchmark.swift:256: the benchmark ignores .rejectedToolCall. This is benchmark-only and sends no data.
- Test stubs (units 54-61): LanguageModel.prepare gains state/prefill and returns .tokens. LaunchAgentRestartTests.swift uses @testable import. These hold no keys or prompts and add no production attack surface.

Limits and open questions. The submodule diffs are not supplied, and 265 replay units are omitted. The pointer bumps change in-process inference code, Metal kernels and the metallib. These run on decrypted prompts and KV state (TB-007, T-028, A-001) and can affect prefix-cache and KV semantics (T-041) and the signed-artifact identity and qualification (T-013, T-034, T-054, TB-011). A later pass should check:
1. Upstream changes do not alter KV/prefix-cache scoping, cacheSalt handling or memory contracts.
2. The production serving path handles the new Generation.rejectedToolCall event without dropping it silently or emitting plaintext (T-008). Only the benchmark handling is visible here.
3. image.source and video.source still cover the .ciImage case, so the post-decode pixel recheck in MediaIngest.swift still runs, and the memory-backed video guarantee (T-050) holds.
4. The platform-side artifact qualification is refreshed for the new metallib. This is outside this repo's scope.
No findings are raised because none is supported by visible evidence. The missing submodule source is a coverage limit, not proof of safety.
